findings.basis: QA writes q1 on the exact surviving non-ok Q for the armed request. M verifies the single canonical q1 against its own forwarded UUID digest and the status on the response actually received before associating validation with D. Exact D must win. The second marker binds the winner and inner status to the M response that survived S03. The host checks its own dispatch result, status, matching unique actor cut, form and mapped site. These conditions distinguish an unmarked same-status stub failure from the marked QA value.
findings.limit: The claim covers marked value provenance on the pinned route. If QA-to-M synthesis or reuse cannot be excluded, at most STUB_NON_OK with publicSite UNKNOWN. If M-to-host synthesis or reuse cannot be excluded, outer and publicSite are UNKNOWN. Copying a valid marker onto a fabricated response is observationally indistinguishable. The transport review and controls are explicit evidence gates.

findings.basis: QA captures the actor epoch before super.fetch, binds R and Q, consumes its slot once, and rejects revoked, sealed or duplicate epochs. M allocates C before S03, ties originalLease and P to C, records D and the wire deadline error for that invocation, and admits B only against the captured P/C and unused entry after parent.finish. The separate deadline label requires the owned lease/C and a matching entry at the existing cut. The matrix covers crossed cells, previously marked foreign responses, re-arm, late returns, duplicate egress and thrown finalizers.

acceptance: The two response observers must run before serialization on the actual mounted paths and preserve fulfillment and rejection, including consuming any derived tap rejection. Treat any path capable of re-emitting an already-marked substitute as unsupported even if the record lookup correctly rejects it. Both requirements are covered by the v2 order, transport and noninterference gates. Their evidence is pending.
